newsitem.title: UK: Copper pulls out of a new dive.
newsitem.headline: Copper pulls out of a new dive.

text.p: The copper price pulled out of its new nosedive on Friday to end just firmer in London but still well below the psychological threshold of $2,000 per tonne.

The market was helped by a drop of 2,100 tonnes in London Metal Exchange warehouse stocks but, even so, trading was volatile before the metal ended at $1,933, up $8 from Thursday. Copper had seemed to be finding a new higher range earlier this week around $2,000 but met heavy speculative selling on Thursday.

The price swings are the biggest in copper since June when Sumitomo Corp of Japan sacked its star trader, Yasuo Hamanaka, alleging he helped run up losses of $1.8 billion in unauthorized trading in copper.
Some traders said the market was harder to navigate now that Hamanaka is no longer active and perceived to be using a huge physical position to help steer prices his way.
Elsewhere in commodity markets, outside the oil sector, coffee prices sank then pared the new losses.
London Robusta futures found bargain-hunters to lift them above new four-week lows of $1,520 a tonne hit early in the day and closed $28 lower at $1,534.
"There is still risk of further downside potential but we saw good industry and roaster support as prices slid," said one trader.

Expectations for higher supply in the 1996/97 period and reports that an Italian court has ruled that Brazil should compensate firms that suffered losses 10 years ago in a joint project to support prices weighed on sentiment.
If the ruling is upheld, Brazil could be transferring 338,739 60-kg bags of coffee, held for years in a Trieste warehouse, to four or five companies.
London cocoa futures rebounded from a new six-month low to end sharply higher on shortcovering and technical buying.
The market was stirred by trade talk that a new crop report by leading trade house Cargill had put the world 1996/97 cocoa deficit at 78,000 tonnes.

The gold market shrugged off stronger-than-expected U.S. jobs data, despite potentially bullish concerns that inflation could be on the rise. London gold closed at $385.55 an ounce, down $0.80 from Thursday.
